ctx.x: Yeah. Next door to that was Tillie's Chicken Shack, where they had the fried chicken and the candied yams and the cornbread -- that was a big thing in New York during that period. Tillie's Chicken Shack. A couple of doors from there was a joint called Mexico's, served like Mexican food, tamales and tacos and.... It was a guy who was half-Black and half-Mexican. I met him -- Mexico. He was a hustler and he... All them people who owned them places were night people.

And down the street were about three or four five joints, what they called juice joints. You'd go down in the basement, knock on the door, the guy would see you (or the woman), and they'd bring you in. And when you go in there, after the smoke clears, you can see maybe two dozen people sitting there, drinkin', smokin', tellin' ghost stories or something, telling lies and just sitting around.
